clue.text: Trouble for Mac or such a braggart

indicators.note: making trouble for these words stirs them up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boastful is causing a headache for a Scotsman called Mac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble for' rearranges MACORSUCHA. Scaramouche is the boastful, cowardly clown of Italian commedia dell'arte.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock character from Italian comedy is a boastful coward, so his name serves for any swaggering boaster.

clue.text: Something to eat, say, when watching the birdie?

explanation.surface: A snack to munch while looking at a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A photographer says 'watch the birdie' and asks the subject to say this word so they smile.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dairy food, and also the word people say to smile for a photograph.

clue.text: Cut off ditch dug by engineers

indicators.note: the ditch is dug by the engineers, so they sit beside it, coming first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps
a ditch is a long narrow trench

explanation.surface: Soldiers excavate a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail or reduce spending is to cut it back, a verb sense matching 'cut off'.

clue.text: Not with stereophonic sound, his obsession?

definitions.text: Not with stereophonic sound, his obsession?

parts.words: Not with stereophonic sound, his obsession?
parts.note: sound that is not stereo is single-channel; a person crazily fixated on one single thing fits that 'single' idea

explanation.surface: Someone who hates stereo recordings is obsessed with that preference.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part suggests MONO; a fanatic with a single fixation is read as a 'mono' maniac.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a single overpowering obsession is described by this term from psychology.

clue.text: Alps, and in Germany, maybe, ground that is 6

indicators.note: 'maybe' suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: the German word for 'and' is und

explanation.surface: The Alps, and some German regions, are examples of elevated terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the answer at 6-down, HIGH, so the definition is 'high ground'. 'maybe' rearranges ALPS plus UND.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilly or mountainous country is elevated terrain, the plural matching 'ground' taken as land generally.

clue.text: This way for the main road

definitions.text: This way for the main road

parts.words: This way for the main road
parts.note: put this word before 'way' and you get a term for a main road

explanation.surface: A signpost points travellers towards the arterial route.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined to 'way' it makes the everyday term for a principal public road.

clue.text: Venetian gentleman's trick in the cattle round-up

indicators.note: the trick is placed in the round-up, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a rodeo was originally a round-up of cattle
to rig something is to fix or trick it

explanation.surface: An Italian nobleman plays a dirty trick during a cowboy event.
explanation.walkthrough: Roderigo is the foolish Venetian gentleman in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello the dupe of Iago is a gentleman of Venice by this name.

clue.text: Of uncertain occurrence in Europe, note

indicators.note: the note is placed within Europe, one inside the other

parts.note: to the British, 'the Continent' means mainland Europe
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Something may or may not happen on the Continent, with a musical touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that depends on chance may or may not happen, so it is conditional and unpredictable.

clue.text: It's completely in Latin

parts.note: the clue describes a two-word Latin phrase meaning 'as a whole'

explanation.surface: Something is written entirely in the language of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a text written wholly in Latin; it is really the Latin for 'completely'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin tag means 'in total' or 'altogether'.

clue.text: "Wither'd murder, Alarum'd by his --, the wolf" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: "Wither'd murder, Alarum'd by his --, the wolf" (Macbeth)

parts.words: Wither'd murder, Alarum'd by his --, the wolf
parts.note: the gap in Macbeth's dagger speech is filled by the watchman whose howl wakes murder

explanation.surface: A quotation from Macbeth's speech before killing Duncan, with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth's 'Is this a dagger' speech, murder is roused by the wolf, its watchman, whose howl is its watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard or lookout keeps watch, and the wolf plays that role for personified murder.

clue.text: These times, in this place, Holy Writ finds a supporter

parts.note: AD, anno domini, labels the years of the present era
here means in this place
NT is the New Testament, part of Holy Writ

explanation.surface: The Bible nowadays gains a follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower who sticks to a cause or leader backs it.

clue.text: Sappers in control of cavalry

parts.note: sappers are military engineers, the RE or Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers are commanding the mounted troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap by which a rider steers a horse is the means of controlling mounted soldiers' horses.

clue.text: Fair money-spinner

parts.note: a fairground ride that literally spins while it earns its owner cash

explanation.surface: Something that makes a decent profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as reasonable and 'money-spinner' as profitable; it is a ride at a funfair that spins and takes money.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round is a revolving fairground ride, a spinner that earns money.

clue.text: Sailor has way of speaking about a renouncement

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: the way of speaking is placed about the a, enclosing it

parts.note: diction is one's manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A seaman's style of talking concerns his giving up of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up a throne or responsibility formally is a relinquishment.

clue.text: Supplier of light cotton material

explanation.surface: A source of illumination made from a cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the string in a taper that burns to give light, and a tufted cotton fabric used for bedspreads.

clue.text: Liberate a Marxist worker

parts.note: the Communist Manifesto says workers have nothing to lose but their fetters, so freeing one means removing those links

explanation.surface: A call to free a communist labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Communist Manifesto ends: workers have nothing to lose but their chains.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone is to release them from fetters.

clue.text: Traverse part of London's East End to find a weapon

parts.note: to traverse is to cross
Bow is a district in East London

explanation.surface: Walk across part of East London to find a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical bow mounted on a stock fires bolts and is a missile weapon.

clue.text: One man in Scotland has eastern plant

parts.note: in Scots, 'one' is ane and 'man' is mon

explanation.surface: A Scotsman owns an Oriental flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The windflower is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Periodical may include explosive material

explanation.surface: A journal might contain a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a regularly published journal, and also a store for ammunition or explosives.

clue.text: Many in Malaga stir this mixture

indicators.note: the many goes in the city name before stirring
stirring mixes these letters up into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Lots of people in the Spanish city of Malaga stir a blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' rearranges MALAGA with M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy of mercury with another metal is a blend, and the word means any combination.

clue.text: Twosome claimed wrongly to be reckoned in dozens

parts.note: a duo is a twosome

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters are in an incorrect order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair made a false claim to be counted by twelves.
explanation.definitionFit: A base-twelve system counts in twelves, so its numbers are reckoned in dozens.

clue.text: An animal to attack

explanation.surface: A creature set on assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A horned farm animal; split into two words it makes 'go at', meaning assault.

clue.text: Recess for fellow supporting a student

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
cove is old British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A break for a man helping out a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook set back into a wall is a small recess.

clue.text: Game for the HQ dance

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A party is held at the headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: America's bat-and-ball sport is a game.

clue.text: A joke Samuel made mincemeat of

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A man named Samuel ruined a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel 15, Samuel hews the Amalekite king in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's King of the Amalekites was hacked to pieces by the prophet Samuel.

clue.text: A support in cooking or riding perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Some help in the kitchen or on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OR plus RIDING. The surface wants 'or riding' to be a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilling frame of metal bars holds food over a fire, so it supports cooking.

clue.text: More work, repairing high-class patio

parts.note: U means upper-class

indicators.note: repairing the paved area puts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: More work is needed to repair the posh terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, whose book describes an ideal island. 'repairing' rearranges PATIO into TOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More's book of 1516 is the famous work by that author.

clue.text: Ring willing to protect the hunted

definitions.note: the definition describes a person employed to protect the hunted

parts.note: game means willing
a keeper is a ring that holds another on the finger

explanation.surface: A ring willing to defend prey.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate warden protects birds and animals that are bred for shooting.
